title: Matthew 10:16–23
context: Jesus widens the mission charge into realism: sheep among wolves, courts and kings, family betrayal, hatred for His name, endurance unto salvation, and flight from town to town until the Son of Man comes. Courage here is Spirit-supplied witness, not naïveté.

voices.heading: Voices from both camps
voices.intro: What earlier interpreters on each side wrote about Matthew 10:16–23.
voices.note: Quotations lightly abridged for length; wording follows standard English translations of the sources named.

arminian.quote: But think not that all your innocence and all your wisdom will screen you from persecution. They will scourge you in their synagogues - In these the Jews held their courts of judicature, about both civil and ecclesiastical affairs. Take no thought - Neither at this time, on any sudden call, need we be careful how or what to answer.
arminian.source: Explanatory Notes upon the New Testament (on Matt 10:16–23)

reformed.quote: Behold, I send you out The exhortation which immediately follows plainly shows the design of this admonition; and therefore the order of the passage must be explained in this manner: "You have need of wisdom and of harmlessness, because you will be like sheep in the midst of wolves " The reason is drawn from the necessity of the case: for if they did not wisely exercise caution, they might be immediately devoured by the wolves; and, on the other hand, if they trembled at the rage of the wolves, or were incautious, they would presently waver, and would at length fail to perform their duty.
reformed.source: Commentary on a Harmony of the Evangelists (on Matt 10:16–23)

verses.text: “Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents and harmless as doves.
verses.arminianNotes:
Behold: the Sender knows the danger. Sheep among wolves need both shrewdness and purity—neither cynicism nor gullibility.

Those in Wesley’s line hear a charge to cultivate wisdom and innocence. Grace enables; disciples remain responsible to walk carefully without becoming wolves themselves.
verses.reformedNotes:
Christ sends into hostility under His care. Serpent-wisdom and dove-innocence are gifts of character for a hostile age.

The “I send” governs the scene. Danger is not accident; mission proceeds under the King’s providence and moral formation.

verses.text: But beware of men, for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you.
verses.arminianNotes:
Beware is pastoral, not paranoid. Religious courts will flog messengers of the kingdom. Expect opposition inside familiar structures.

Clear eyes protect soft hearts. Knowing the cost helps disciples choose faithfulness when pressure comes.
verses.reformedNotes:
Men will hand over; synagogues will flog. Conflict is foretold so faith is not shocked into collapse.

Jesus scripts the trouble before it arrives. Suffering for the gospel is not outside His plan.

verses.text: Yes, and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.
verses.arminianNotes:
Civil power becomes a pulpit. “For my sake” and to bear witness redefine humiliation as opportunity toward rulers and Gentiles.

Arminians stress the purpose: testimony offered so hearers may believe. Even coercion can open doors for a free gospel invitation.
verses.reformedNotes:
The disciples will be dragged before rulers, yet for a purpose. Witness before governors and Gentiles is the Father’s stage for the Son’s name.

Persecution advances mission. What enemies intend for silence, God turns into proclamation under His decree.

verses.text: But when they deliver you up, don’t be anxious how or what you will say, for it will be given you in that hour what you will say.
verses.arminianNotes:
Anxiety about words is forbidden because help is promised in the hour. Prepare a life of faith; trust timely speech.

The promise invites dependence, not laziness. God supplies what obedience needs when the crisis comes.
verses.reformedNotes:
Deliverance to courts meets deliverance of words. “Will be given” is divine provision in the crisis moment.

The Spirit’s timing is perfect. Anxiety yields because God Himself undertakes the testimony.

verses.text: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
verses.arminianNotes:
The Father’s Spirit speaks through willing messengers. Human agency remains; the power is divine.

Arminians treasure this cooperation: disciples open their mouths; the Spirit fills them. Both confess: witness is Spirit-empowered, never mere rhetoric.
verses.reformedNotes:
Ultimate speaker: the Spirit of your Father. Apostolic courage is Trinitarian help.

God does not abandon His witnesses. Through them He Himself addresses courts and kings.
verses.keyContrast: Both confess Spirit-empowered speech. Arminians emphasize grace-enabled human speaking; Reformed Christians highlight that God Himself is the decisive speaker through His servants.

verses.text: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.
verses.arminianNotes:
Family ties fracture under allegiance to Jesus. Love of kin does not excuse betrayal of the truth—or guarantee loyalty to it.

Choose Christ even when homes divide. The gospel’s claim is personal and costly.
verses.reformedNotes:
Domestic hatred is prophesied, not celebrated. The sword of division (vv. 34–36) already casts its shadow.

Sin’s reach into households shows how deep the conflict with the King runs. Endurance will need more than natural affection.

verses.text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
verses.arminianNotes:
Hatred “for my name’s sake” marks true discipleship. Salvation is promised to those who endure—perseverance is necessary and grace-enabled.

The disciples must endure and not quit. God’s grace sustains, and believers must continue. Final salvation and present faithfulness belong together.
verses.reformedNotes:
Universal hostility for the Name, then the promise: endurance to the end marks the saved.

Those God saves He keeps, and He keeps them in the path of endurance. Perseverance is fruit of grace, not a human ladder to earn life.
verses.keyContrast: Both require endurance and reject cheap discipleship. Arminians emphasize necessary, grace-enabled continuance that can be forsaken; Reformed readers stress that the elect will endure because God preserves them to the end.

verses.text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next, for most certainly I tell you, you will not have gone through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man has come.
verses.arminianNotes:
Flight is permitted wisdom, not cowardice. Keep moving with the message. The Son of Man’s coming presses urgency on Israel’s towns.

Use prudence; keep proclaiming. Timing language fuels mission zeal without licensing despair.
verses.reformedNotes:
Fleeing town to town is commanded strategy under persecution. The “most certainly” promise ties Israel’s unfinished circuit to the Son of Man’s coming (debated as AD 70, resurrection, or consummation—Matthew’s point is certainty and urgency).

Christ’s coming governs the calendar of mission. Messengers are not to seek martyrdom for its own sake; they are to finish the assigned circuit under His lordship.
